key_insight: Frozen weights need no writes or refresh: a DUV-only NOR/via-ROM die (~25 masks, no capacitor, no EUV) at ~800 nm2/bit matches 1b density, with zero read disturb unlike HBF NAND.
killer_doubt: E-beam writing ~2-4e13 vias per wafer takes tens of hours; use a ~$0.3M ArF via mask per model instead. Real doubt: fleet model life under ~12 months strands frozen silicon.
decisive_experiment: 28 nm MPW NOR-ROM macro with via-size 2-bit cells: measure read margin and access time across corners; in parallel, a $/GB model at SAQP F=20 nm versus HBF including read-disturb rewrite budgets.
prior_art: Mask ROM (1970s); YOLoC ROM-CIM (DAC 2022); SanDisk High Bandwidth Flash for weights (2025); Taalas hardwired-model chips (2026). All from memory, unverified.

key_insight: Charge moves through a semiconductor channel, not a tunnel oxide, so wear is gate stress only; no per-bit transistor, capacitor or staircase (phases share plates); bits added by deposition.
killer_doubt: imec planar IGZO CCD CTE is >98%; need >=99.99% (0.98^128 keeps 7.5%). imec's 3D clocks >4 MHz, so a 64-stage shift takes ~16 us, not 100-300 ns.
decisive_experiment: University-fab planar 4-phase IGZO CCDs, surface versus buried-channel (IGO/IGZO heterostructure) with fat-zero bias; measure CTE versus clock (4-200 MHz) at 25-85 C. Go if >=0.9999 at >=50 MHz.
prior_art: imec IEDM 2024 planar IGZO CCD (CTE>98%, >200 s retention, >1e10 cycles); imec IMW 2026 vertical 3D CCD (via search snippet); 1970s Si CCD memories.

key_insight: Shows W, Hf, Zr, In and Ga are not physically required; a chokepoint-free element list is a useful resilience constraint for any U.S. memory flow.
killer_doubt: Poly-Si TFT off-current ~0.1-1 pA versus the 13 fA tail: a 1 fF node keeps 0.2 V only ~0.2-2 ms. Contact-litho density is ~1e4-1e5x below 1b.
decisive_experiment: No device run needed; it would reproduce 1970s data. Cheaper: a paper audit of which chokepoint elements DRAM truly needs (W to Mo/Ru, Hf to Zr), costed per wafer.
prior_art: 1970s 3T/2T gain-cell DRAM (Intel 1103 3T cell); modern Si gain-cell eDRAM; poly-Si TFT memory studies.

key_insight: Attention scores tolerate low precision, so an MSB-first bit-plane layout screens most KV values with a fraction of the bits fetched.
killer_doubt: Real gain ~2-3x, not 8-12x: INT8 with 4 MSB planes plus 10% low-plane refetch moves 55% of bits (1.8x); FP16 ~3x. SpAtten already does this.
decisive_experiment: Software trace study: replay LLM attention over real KV caches with MSB-plane screening; measure bits fetched per token at iso-accuracy. About a GPU-week.
prior_art: SpAtten (HPCA 2021) progressive quantization fetches MSBs first and LSBs on demand; bit-serial accelerators (Stripes, Bit-Pragmatic). From memory.

key_insight: Coax arithmetic is right: 1 nm core, 2 nm k~35 shell gives ~1.8 fF/um geometric, and a grown AR-100 pillar avoids the fluorocarbon HAR etch.
killer_doubt: SWCNT quantum capacitance ~0.4 fF/um in series cuts it to ~0.33 fF/um; inner-surface field ~9 MV/cm at 1 V; one tube per site at 10 nm pitch, 1.7e10/die, unshown.
decisive_experiment: Grow vertical SWCNTs from e-beam-defined Fe dots at 20-40 nm pitch on TiN; count single-tube-per-site yield over 1e6 sites. Below ~99.99%, drop permanently.
prior_art: CNT-forest MIM capacitors in academia; CNT vias (Infineon, imec). No single-tube DRAM storage capacitor found. From memory.

key_insight: Stranded DRAM is real: servers are provisioned for peak per socket, so pooling recovers capacity without new wafers.
killer_doubt: Microsoft's Pond found ~7% DRAM saving at 16-socket pools, not 20-30%; rack-scale CXL adds ~150-300 ns, and minute-scale leasing needs live page migration.
decisive_experiment: Replay public Azure/Google cluster traces through a pooling simulator for savings versus pool size and latency; largely already done by Pond.
prior_art: Microsoft Pond (ASPLOS 2023); Google far memory (ASPLOS 2019); commercial CXL pooling appliances. From memory.

key_insight: DRAM has no wear-out, so retired DIMMs are near-new; retention re-binning, per-bin refresh and CXL-side ECC turn scrap into far memory at ~$0.3-1/GB.
killer_doubt: Supply ceiling: server DRAM shipped ~2021, now retiring, is ~6-10% of 2026 bit demand even if a third party captures 30-50%; hyperscalers already reuse it internally.
decisive_experiment: Buy 1,000 retired DDR4 RDIMMs; profile retention, VRT and row-hammer at 85 C; build a CXL-card prototype; measure usable-GB yield and W/GB versus new DDR5.
prior_art: Microsoft GreenSKU (ISCA 2024) reuses DDR4 behind CXL; secondary DIMM brokers. From memory.

key_insight: Water claim checks out: ~8 m3 per wafer over 3,068 GB is ~2.6 L/GB (~0.33 L/Gb), so a reused bit avoids almost all fab water.
killer_doubt: Duplicate of I-06172; robotic desoldering and reballing adds rework loss and cost versus reusing whole DIMMs, which are already socketed.
decisive_experiment: Folded into I-06172's test; add a 500-package desolder, reball and retest run to price rework yield loss.
prior_art: Same as I-06172: GreenSKU, used-DIMM brokers.

key_insight: Cost framing is right: marginal reuse cost is test, card and controller, far below 4x-inflated new DRAM.
killer_doubt: Duplicate of I-06172; $0.05-0.15/GB is low, since a CXL Type-3 controller card (~$150-300 per 256-512 GB) alone is ~$0.3-1/GB, still ~20x under $20/GB.
decisive_experiment: Folded into I-06172; obtain controller-card BOM quotes and retired-DIMM auction prices to fix the $/GB band.
prior_art: Same as I-06172: GreenSKU, used-DIMM brokers.

key_insight: Right scale shift: retire the server, keep the DIMMs, and serve them through a mature-node CXL bridge.
killer_doubt: Duplicate of I-06172 and already deployed; a 150-250 ns tier suits only cold pages (~20-30% of footprint), capping how much new DDR5 it displaces.
decisive_experiment: Folded into I-06172; measure the cold-page fraction on target workloads to bound displaced DDR5.
prior_art: Microsoft GreenSKU (ISCA 2024) DDR4 behind CXL. From memory.

key_insight: Display fabs are depreciated, EUV- and crucible-free, and know IGZO; a Gen-8.5 panel is ~78x a 300 mm wafer. B2-19 imprint at F~100 nm is the real revival.
killer_doubt: At 2 um rules a ~30F2 cell is ~120 um2/bit: six layers give ~17 GB/panel versus 3,068 GB per 1b wafer, so ~$30-90/GB versus $1.48.
decisive_experiment: One-week cost model with a panel maker's cash cost per mask-layer per m2; reaching $1.48/GB even at F=1 um needs under ~$0.6 per m2-mask. Expect failure.
prior_art: ram-venture A1-03 killed display-glass IGZO memory at 2 um on density; memory-in-pixel LCDs (Sharp, JDI); SEL CAAC-IGZO memories.

key_insight: An on-package retention and wear log makes die-level reuse traceable; solderless attach matters for soldered LPDDR and CAMM systems.
killer_doubt: DIMMs are already socketed, and a DDR5 die cannot speak DDR6; only a CXL bridge enables cross-generation reuse, which works on whole DIMMs anyway.
decisive_experiment: Signal-integrity test of a compression-LGA DRAM package at 6.4-8.5 Gb/s, plus a cost model of ~16 sockets per module against second-life value.
prior_art: JEDEC CAMM2/LPCAMM2 compression-attach modules (2023); socketed BGA test sockets. From memory.
